# KSFAssistant toolchain integration

The official lark-* sibling Skills contain the domain instructions. Read the relevant official Skill; do not replace its business guidance with this integration note. The app bundles CLI and Skills from the same pinned v1.0.93 tag. No automatic updates or online skill installation.

## Managed CLI

On macOS the absolute launcher is `~/.local/share/ksfassistant/toolchain/bin/ksfas-lark`; on Windows it is `%USERPROFILE%/AppData/Local/KSFAssistant/toolchain/bin/ksfas-lark.exe`. Expand the user's home path, quote the executable path, and substitute it for `lark-cli` in official Skill commands. A same-directory `lark-cli` alias is also managed; adding this directory to PATH is an explicit user choice, never an automatic agent edit. Do not overwrite any other installed CLI.

The launcher resolves the configured app bundle and fixed default profile, feishu brand, and configuration directory, reusing the official local credential store. All business operations enforce the shared local capability policy. Supported user reads and bot operations do not require the desktop; disabled capabilities remain disabled. User writes require the running, unlocked KSFAssistant desktop and a one-time native approval. Never export, copy, print, or inject app secrets, user tokens, or credentials into argv, environment, logs, or Skills. Profile/config-dir overrides and self-update/skill-install commands are refused.

## Available managed capabilities

Before an unfamiliar business command, run the managed launcher with `managed capabilities --json`. This local inventory describes the pinned execution contract, supported commands, parameter restrictions and intentional limitations; it does not read credentials, grant permissions or call Feishu. Use the official domain Skill and preserve its URL, view, pagination and output semantics. Local help/schema discovery is not proof that a business action is authorized. Never interpret a managed restriction as a missing platform scope or work around it by changing identity, using another executable, or calling an arbitrary API. Official script/dynamic workflow and independent event-consumer restrictions remain explicit.

## Download and export results

When a result contains `artifactDelivery`, use the absolute `artifacts[*].path` as the canonical delivered files, with `bytes` and `sha256` for verification. Upstream fields such as `record_file` or `manifest_file` may refer to removed staging paths; do not use them instead of `artifacts`. Non-object upstream output is preserved under `upstreamOutput`. A failed invocation with `partialArtifacts` or partial artifact delivery is not success and must not be replayed automatically. Base NDJSON has a sibling `.manifest.json`; preserve its view scope, revision and pagination markers and never infer completeness only from a successful exit.

## Authorization and repair

Prefer KSFAssistant's Feishu authorization settings to configure an application, show the QR authorization flow, inspect status, or clear authorization through an explicit user action. Read-only auth status/scopes remain available without the GUI; configure, login and recovery use the desktop authorization settings. Missing authorization is not permission to inspect credential files. If the bundle moved or an owned Skill was edited, explain the error and use the app's explicit toolchain management action; do not bypass ownership checks or remove user changes.

## User-identity write approval

Always specify exactly one `--as user` or `--as bot` on business commands. Reviewed user reads do not prompt. User create/send/upload/update/delete and membership/sharing/permission changes wait for one native desktop decision; old disabled capabilities remain disabled. Do not add `--yes`, approved/challenge flags, change identity, bypass the managed executable, or automate clicking the approval button. Denial, close, timeout, unavailable/locked desktop, changed identity/input/policy or unsupported command is a stop, not permission to retry through another route. An unknown result after execution must be inspected read-only; do not replay. Consult the managed inventory for command/parameter support. Report intentional restrictions, invalid input, missing authorization, platform permission failures and unknown outcomes distinctly. After an application upgrade, a changed execution manifest or stale launcher requires the explicit managed toolchain upgrade; never patch the receipt or installed Skills by hand. File/stdin inputs are frozen before prompting; large or dynamically expanding inputs can be refused. Different real writes in a compound business operation can require separate decisions.

## Independent task CLI

The stable user entry is `~/.local/share/ksfassistant/toolchain/bin/ksf-assistant-task` on macOS and `%USERPROFILE%/AppData/Local/KSFAssistant/toolchain/bin/ksf-assistant-task.exe` on Windows. It forwards stdin, arguments and exit status without Core. The app resource is `runtime/task/<platform>/ksf-assistant-task` (`.exe` on Windows), where platform is darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, windows-arm64, or windows-x64. It supports report/get/list/doctor independently of Core. Use its versioned stdin JSON contract; do not invent task identity, route verification receipts, revisions, or credentials. Task-reporting policy and KSF Skill registration are managed separately.
